newsitem.title: UK: BBC confirms it will launch digital terrestrial tv.
newsitem.headline: BBC confirms it will launch digital terrestrial tv.

text.p: The BBC on Tuesday confirmed it would launch free-to-air digital terrestrial television services, taking a guaranteed place on a digital terrestrial multiplex offered by the Department of National Heritage.
The BBC and other maintstream television broadcasters in the UK have all been offered access to multiplexes, which are a bundle of digital channels, for the launch of digital terrestrial television.
There will be three-and-a-half other multiplexes which will be advertised and auctioned off by the Independent Television Commission.
Licences for these should be granted next summer.
The BBC said in a statement it intended to use the multiplex to offer its BBC1 and BBC2 main channels in widescreen format along with a 24-hour BBC News service.
It would also offer additional regional and educational programming. The BBC aims to make its digital services available on all distribution systems, including terrestrial, satellite and cable.
